papers.title_in_file: The Power of One Clean Qubit in Supervised Machine Learning
papers.what_it_is: Uses the DQC1 one-clean-qubit model to estimate kernels for supervised classification, run on IBM hardware.

assertions.value: The authors report that the DQC1 kernel classifies the ad_hoc dataset with 100% accuracy on the Qiskit simulator and 90% on IBM hardware.
quotes: From Fig. (5), it can be seen that the accuracy of the Qiskit simulator is 100%. On the other hand, the obtained accuracy on the hardware is 90%.
assertions.certainty_reason: One dataset, one device (single study).
assertions.reader_inference: The 10 point gap is attributed by the authors to hardware noise.

assertions.value: The authors state that the number of measurements the DQC1 kernel needs scales exponentially with the number of target qubits, and they expect the same untrainability issues as for other quantum kernels.
quotes: the number of required measurements scales exponentially with the number of target qubits, as the variance in the kernel exponentially approaches zero.
Hence, we expect the same untrainability issues to hold for our kernel function.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state their own limit, Discussion p.8.

assertions.value: The authors report empirical results on three datasets that support the idea that higher purity of the control qubit raises the accuracy of the DQC1 kernel model.
quotes: support the idea that improving the purity of the control qubit
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on three datasets.

papers.title_in_file: Protocols for classically training quantum generative models on probability distributions
papers.what_it_is: Proposes classical training of IQP-type quantum generative models while sampling stays classically hard.

assertions.value: The authors report numerical end-to-end training of IQP circuits on probability distributions for up to 30 qubits on a regular desktop computer.
quotes: We numerically demonstrate the end-to-end training of IQP circuits using probability distributions for up to 30 qubits on a regular desktop computer.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result of this study.
assertions.reader_inference: Classical training cost is shown only for the distributions the authors chose.

assertions.value: The authors state that they examine anti-concentration for systems of up to 20 qubits, and for larger registers they use cross-entropy difference against the Porter-Thomas distribution.
quotes: We use the approach discussed above for studying systems with up 20 qubits. For larger number of qubits we use the fact that the probability distributions converge to the PorterThomas distribution
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope of the hardness check.
assertions.reader_inference: The Conclusion says 16 qubits for the same check, so the paper gives two figures (20 and 16).

assertions.value: The authors state that the worst-case training difficulty reported in other work does not arise for their method because they assume knowledge of the target probability distribution.
quotes: in our case, however this issue does not arise since we are assuming knowledge of the target probability distribution.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper states its own setup assumption, Sec. IV.

papers.title_in_file: Analyzing the quantum approximate optimization algorithm: ansatze, symmetries, and Lie algebras
papers.what_it_is: Characterizes Lie algebras of QAOA ansatze for maxcut and links their size to barren plateaus.

assertions.value: The authors report that the Lie algebras of the multi-angle ansatz fall into six families, and for every connected graph except cycle and path graphs the Lie dimension is exponentially large in the system size.
quotes: fully characterize the Lie algebras of the multi-angle ansatz across arbitrary connected graphs, finding that they only fall into one of just six families.
Besides the cycle and the path graphs, the Lie dimensions for every graph are exponentially large in the system size
assertions.certainty_reason: Main result of the paper, Abstract and Sec. XI; proofs in the appendices.
assertions.reader_inference: The authors infer multi-angle ansatze are extremely prone to barren plateaus.

assertions.value: The authors conjecture that for most graphs the standard Lie algebras have only components that are exponential or grow at most polynomially with the system size.
quotes: we conjecture that (for most graphs) the standard Lie algebras have only components that are either exponential or that grow, at most, polynomially with the system size.
assertions.certainty_reason: A conjecture, not proved in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: If true, the authors say QAOA is prone to barren plateaus or classically simulable.

assertions.value: The authors state that barren plateaus have been shown only for the multi-angle ansatz, and that barren plateaus are an average statement for randomly initialized circuits.
quotes: Even though barren plateaus have only been shown for the multi-angle ansatz
barren plateaus are an average statement that hold for randomly initialized circuits
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state the limit of their own result, Sec. XI.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum machine learning with subspace states
papers.what_it_is: Introduces quantum subspace states and algorithms for determinant sampling, compound-matrix singular value estimation and topological data analysis.

assertions.value: The paper states in Theorem 1.3 that a quantum determinant sampling algorithm exists with O(nd2) pre-processing and circuits with O(nd log n) gates and total depth O(d log n).
quotes: there is a quantum determinant sampling algorithm that requires O(nd2) pre-processing to orthogonalize A, and generates subsequent samples using a quantum circuit with O(nd log n) gates and with total depth O(d log n).
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1.3, restated as Theorem 5.5.

assertions.value: The authors state that for d = O(n) the quantum determinant sampling algorithm has gate complexity O(n2) against O(n3) for the state-of-the-art classical algorithm.
quotes: For the case d = O(n), the quantum determinant sampling algorithm has gate complexity O(n2) compared to the state-of-the-art classical algorithm with gate complexity O(n3).
assertions.certainty_reason: Comparison depends on a cited classical bound.

assertions.value: The authors state that for matrices of low Givens complexity it remains to be seen if more efficient classical determinant sampling algorithms exist.
quotes: it remains to be seen if more efficient classical determinant sampling algorithms can be given for this setting.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state an open point about their own claimed speedup.

papers.title_in_file: Scalable Imaginary Time Evolution with Neural Network Quantum States
papers.what_it_is: Trains neural network quantum states by imaginary time evolution with first-order gradient descent.

assertions.value: The authors report numerical experiments on a Heisenberg model on a square lattice that show higher stability and final energy accuracy than direct energy loss minimization.
quotes: providing compelling evidence that our method offers higher stability and final energy accuracy than the optimization of NQS with energy as a loss function.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result on one model.

assertions.value: The authors state that their numerical experiments were performed without leveraging the symmetries of the physical system.
quotes: We emphasize that our numerical experiments were performed without leveraging the symmetries of the physical system
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state their own experimental setup.

assertions.value: The authors suggest that unstable convergence with energy loss may arise from a constantly shifting target.
quotes: The instability might arise due to a constantly shifting target.
assertions.certainty_reason: A hypothesis, stated as possible.

papers.title_in_file: Layering and subpool exploration for adaptive Variational Quantum Eigensolvers
papers.what_it_is: Studies layering of ADAPT-VQE circuits and a subpool exploration subroutine, with noise simulations.

assertions.value: The authors report that layering improves noise resilience with respect to amplitude-damping and dephasing noise.
quotes: We find that layering leads to an improved noise resilience with respect to amplitude-damping and dephasing noise, which, in general, affect idling and non-idling qubits alike.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulation of small molecules.

assertions.value: The authors report no advantage of layering with respect to depolarizing noise.
quotes: With respect to depolarizing noise, which tends to affect only actively manipulated qubits, we observe no advantage of layering.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulation result.

assertions.value: The authors state that in the studied examples subpool exploration had little impact, and that this could change for larger molecules.
quotes: Thus, subpool exploration had little impact on the algorithms.
Again, this could change when larger molecules are studied.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state the limit of their own result, Sec. VII.

papers.title_in_file: Towards Efficient Quantum Computing for Quantum Chemistry
papers.what_it_is: Combines the transcorrelated method with adaptive ansatze (TC-AVQITE) for small molecules.

assertions.value: The authors report close agreement with complete basis set limit results despite using a minimal basis set, in contrast to traditional non-transcorrelated methods.
quotes: we demonstrate a close agreement with complete basis set limit results despite using a minimal basis set; in stark contrast to traditional (non-transcorrelated) methods.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation of three small molecules.

assertions.value: The authors report that for the systems studied, TC with adaptive ansatze reduces required quantum resources by a factor of 5 to 10 compared to the fixed ansatz strategy TC-VarQITE.
quotes: reduces the required quantum resources by a factor of 5 to 10 compared to a fixed quantum ansatz strategy employed in TC-VarQITE.
assertions.certainty_reason: Result on the systems studied only.

assertions.value: The authors state that the study covers small molecular systems, namely H4, LiH and H2O, and that hardware noise effects are left for future work.
quotes: The combined TC-AVQITE method is used to calculate ground state energies across the potential energy surfaces of H4, LiH, and H2O.
While the current study focuses on small molecular systems
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state their own scope.

papers.title_in_file: The generative quantum eigensolver (GQE) and its application for ground state search
papers.what_it_is: Proposes GQE, a transformer-based generator of quantum circuits for ground state search.

assertions.value: The authors report that for N2 GPT-QE achieves higher accuracy than CCSD across most bond lengths.
quotes: Notably, for N2, GPT-QE achieves higher accuracy than CCSD across most bond lengths, particularly in the equilibrium region
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result on a few molecules.

assertions.value: The authors report that chemical accuracy is maintained near the equilibrium geometry but deteriorates in the bond dissociation region.
quotes: chemical accuracy is maintained near the equilibrium geometry, but deteriorates in the bond dissociation region where the electronic structure becomes more complex.
assertions.certainty_reason: The molecule this sentence covers is not named in the quoted paragraph.

assertions.value: The authors state that experiments with larger molecules are required and that the work is a proof of concept.
quotes: Many other research directions should be explored to fully enable the GPT-QE models to progress beyond this proof of concept.
experiments with larger molecules are required to further assess the optimization behavior.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state their own limit, Sec. 4.
